ELECTRONICS CARE PLAN
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 1

1. Definitions
1.1. Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
1.2. Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
1.3. Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by us.
1.4. Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
1.5. Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
1.6. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.7. Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.8. Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.
1.9. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.10. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.11. Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
1.12. Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

2. Limits and service fee
2.1. Accidental Damage: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
2.2. Breakdown: limit $1,000 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
2.3. Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
2.4. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

3. Breakdown
3.1. We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
3.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
3.3. The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
3.4. We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
3.5. We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

4. Communication
4.1. We will communicate with you in English.
4.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

5. Cooperation
5.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
5.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

6. Transferring the plan
6.1. You may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling us in writing.
6.2. The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

7. Assignment
7.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

8. Governing law
8.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
8.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

9. Data protection
9.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
9.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
9.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

10. Interpretation
10.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
10.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
10.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

11. Instalment agreements
11.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
11.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

12. Waiver
12.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

13. Accidental Damage
13.1. We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
13.2. The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
13.3. The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $250 per incident.
13.4. We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
13.5. We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

14. Repair process
14.1. After a claim is accepted, we will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
14.2. We aim to return repaired devices within 10 business days of receiving them.

15. Inflation
15.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
15.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

16. Data and backups
16.1. We are not responsible for recovering or restoring any data, software or settings stored on your device.
16.2. You should back up your data regularly and before sending the device for repair.

17. Taxes
17.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
17.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

18. Change of address
18.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
18.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

19. Exchange of information
19.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
19.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

20. Market conditions
20.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

21. Software support
21.1. Our helpline can give advice on setting up and using your device.
21.2. Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

22. Claims documents
22.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
22.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

23. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
23.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

24. Geographical limits
24.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
24.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

25. Automatic renewal
25.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
25.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

26. Cancellation
26.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
26.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
26.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

27. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
27.1. We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
27.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
27.3. The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
27.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
27.5. We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

28. Severability
28.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

29. Subrogation
29.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
29.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

30. Accessibility
30.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

31. Renewal
31.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
31.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

32. Records and evidence
32.1. You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
32.2. Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
32.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

33. Electronic documents
33.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
33.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
33.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

34. Payment of claims
34.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
34.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

35. Notices
35.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
35.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

36. Third-party administrators
36.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
36.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

37. General exclusions
37.1. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
37.2. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
37.3. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
37.4. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
37.5. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

38. Making a claim
38.1. You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
38.2. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
38.3. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

39. Duty of fair presentation
39.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
39.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
39.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

40. Changes in circumstances
40.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
40.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

41. Interest
41.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

42. How to read this document
42.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
42.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
42.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

43. Arbitration
43.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
43.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

44. Replacement devices
44.1. If we cannot repair your device economically, we will replace it with a replacement device.
44.2. Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
44.3. Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

45. Unrecoverable devices
45.1. If a device is found after we have replaced it, the found device becomes our property and must be sent to us.
45.2. We may block devices reported as lost or stolen so that they cannot be used on mobile networks.

46. Discounts
46.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
46.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

47. Recovery of costs
47.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

48. Compensation scheme
48.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
48.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

49. Customer support
49.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
49.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

50. Reasonable precautions
50.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
50.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

51. Complaints
51.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
51.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
51.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

52. Sanctions
52.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

53. Fraud
53.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
53.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

54. Joint policyholders
54.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
54.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

55. Currency
55.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
55.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

56. Environmental commitment
56.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
56.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

57. Salvage
57.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
57.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

58. Premium payment
58.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
58.2. If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

59. Other insurance
59.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
59.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 2

1. Definitions
1.1. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.2. Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
1.3. Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
1.4. Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
1.5. Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
1.6. Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.

2. Limits and deductible
2.1. Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.2. Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $40 per claim.
2.3. Therapy Services: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.4. Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $100 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

3. Subrogation
3.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
3.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

4. Complaints
4.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
4.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
4.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

5. Market conditions
5.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

6. Therapy Services
6.1. We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
6.2. The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
6.3. We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
6.4. We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

7. Dental Care
7.1. We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
7.2. No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
7.3. The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.
7.4. The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $600 per treatment.
7.5. We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
7.6. We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

8. Geographical limits
8.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
8.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

9. Arbitration
9.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
9.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

10. Claims documents
10.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
10.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

11. Appeals
11.1. If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
11.2. An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
11.3. We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

12. Optional cover: Hearing Care
12.1. We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
12.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
12.3. The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
12.4. We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

13. Customer support
13.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
13.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

14. General exclusions
14.1. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
14.2. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
14.3. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

15. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
15.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

16. Exchange of information
16.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
16.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

17. Making a claim
17.1. You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
17.2. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
17.3. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

18. Eligibility
18.1. Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
18.2. Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

19. Other insurance
19.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
19.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

20. Cooperation
20.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
20.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

21. Automatic renewal
21.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
21.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

=== CLAIM ===
Customer (Noah): Hi, I need to make a claim on policy T560527 under Dental Care for a crown.
Agent: Sure. When did the policy start and what covers does your schedule show?
Customer (Noah): It started on Friday, October 17, 2025. The schedule lists Dental Care, Vision Care, Therapy Services, Hearing Care, and extensions: none.
Agent: When did the treatment happen, and what happened?
Customer (Noah): On Thursday, December 4, 2025. The dentist recommended the treatment after a routine check-up.
Agent: Anything else we should know?
Customer (Noah): The provider issued an itemised invoice. Noah joined the company's finance team two years ago.
Agent: Noted. I am logging this claim today, Monday, December 8, 2025, the first time it has been reported to us. Our adjuster has assessed the loss at $958.

DEVICE PROTECTION PLAN TERMS
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 1

1. Definitions
1.1. Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
1.2. Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
1.3. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any service fee, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.4. Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by us.
1.5. Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
1.6. Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 12 months after the device was bought.
1.7. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.8. Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.9. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.10. Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
1.11. Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.12. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.13. Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

2. Limits and service fee
2.1. Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
2.2. Breakdown: limit $1,500 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
2.3. Theft and Loss: limit $800 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
2.4. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

3. Accidental Damage
3.1. We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
3.2. The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
3.3. The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $250 per incident.
3.4. We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
3.5. We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

4. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
4.1. We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
4.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
4.3. The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
4.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
4.5. We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

5. Breakdown
5.1. We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
5.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
5.3. The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
5.4. We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
5.5. We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

6. General exclusions
6.1. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
6.2. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
6.3. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
6.4. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

7. Making a claim
7.1. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
7.2. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
7.3. You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

8. Geographical limits
8.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
8.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

9. Claims documents
9.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
9.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

10. Complaints
10.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
10.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
10.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

11. Transferring the plan
11.1. You may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling us in writing.
11.2. The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

12. Accessibility
12.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

13. Inflation
13.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
13.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

14. Discounts
14.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
14.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

15. Joint policyholders
15.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
15.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

16. Fraud
16.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
16.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

17. How to read this document
17.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
17.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
17.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

18. Third-party administrators
18.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
18.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

19. Replacement devices
19.1. If we cannot repair your device economically, we will replace it with a replacement device.
19.2. Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
19.3. Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

20. Changes in circumstances
20.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
20.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

21. Taxes
21.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
21.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

22. Recovery of costs
22.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

23. Duty of fair presentation
23.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
23.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
23.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

24. Premium payment
24.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
24.2. If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

25. Exchange of information
25.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
25.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

26. Salvage
26.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
26.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

27. Electronic documents
27.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
27.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
27.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

28. Compensation scheme
28.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
28.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

29. Change of address
29.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
29.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

30. Governing law
30.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
30.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

31. Other insurance
31.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
31.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

32. Software support
32.1. Our helpline can give advice on setting up and using your device.
32.2. Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

33. Renewal

49. Cooperation

49.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

50. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)

51. Severability

52. Assignment

Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 3

1. Definitions
1.1. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.2. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.3. Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
1.4. Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
1.5. Hearing aid replacement period means 24 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
1.6. Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.7. Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
1.8. Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
1.9. Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
1.10. Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
1.11. Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
1.12. Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
1.13. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.14. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.15. Replacement period means 12 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.

2.4. Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

3. Inflation

3.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

33.3. The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $750 per treatment.

36.2. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
36.3. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
36.4. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
36.5. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

37.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.

44. Electronic documents
44.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.

SINGLE-TRIP TRAVEL PROTECTION PLAN
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 3

1. Definitions
1.1. Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
1.2. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.3. Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
1.4. Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
2.2. Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $50,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.3. Trip Cancellation: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.4. Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

3. Trip Cancellation
3.1. We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
3.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
3.3. The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
3.4. We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
3.5. We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

4. Cancellation
4.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
4.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
4.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

5. Claims documents
5.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
5.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

6. Accessibility
6.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

7. Baggage and Personal Belongings
7.1. We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
7.2. The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
7.3. The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
7.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
7.5. We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
7.6. We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

8. Severability
8.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

9. Instalment agreements
9.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
9.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

10. Rental car excess
10.1. If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
10.2. This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

11. General exclusions
11.1. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
11.2. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

12. Making a claim
12.1. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
12.2. You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
12.3. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

13. Joint policyholders
13.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
13.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

14. Repatriation
14.1. If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
14.2. We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

15. Electronic documents
15.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
15.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
15.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

16. Complaints
16.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
16.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
16.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

17. Currency
17.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
17.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

18. Exchange of information
18.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
18.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

=== CLAIM ===
Customer (Elin): Hi, I need to make a claim on policy P346410 under Trip Cancellation for non-refundable flights and hotel bookings.
Agent: Sure. When did the policy start and what covers does your schedule show?
Customer (Elin): It started on Sunday, October 5, 2025. The schedule lists Baggage and Personal Belongings, Emergency Medical Expenses, Trip Cancellation, and extensions: none.
Agent: When did the incident happen, and what happened?
Customer (Elin): On Wednesday, October 22, 2025. Elin cancelled after receiving a jury summons for the travel dates.
Agent: Anything else we should know?
Customer (Elin): The destination was a coastal town Elin had visited before. The trip was booked through an online travel agent. Elin was travelling with two colleagues.
Agent: Noted. I am logging this claim today, Thursday, December 18, 2025, the first time it has been reported to us. Our adjuster has assessed the loss at $2,328.

1. Definitions
1.1. Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
1.2. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.3. Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.

1.5. Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
1.6. Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
1.7. High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
1.8. Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
1.9. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.10. Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
1.11. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.12. Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.13. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.14. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.15. Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 60 consecutive days.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.2. Escape of Water: limit $30,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.3. Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4. Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

3. Other insurance
3.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
3.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

4. Third-party administrators
4.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
4.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

5. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
5.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

6. Change of address
6.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
6.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

7. Tenant's improvements
7.1. If you rent the home, we will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that you installed and are responsible for.
7.2. This cover applies only to improvements you paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

8. Freezer contents
8.1. We will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
8.2. We will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

9. Theft
9.1. We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
9.2. The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,500 per incident.
9.3. The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
9.4. We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
9.5. We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
9.6. We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

10. Exchange of information
10.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.

11.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

12. Reasonable precautions
12.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
12.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

13. Currency
13.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
13.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

17.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.

18. Changes in circumstances
18.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.

19. Claims documents
19.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
19.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

20. Accessibility
20.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

21.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.

22.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
22.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

23.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.

25.3. The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.

25.5. We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

26.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
26.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.

27.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.

54.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.

55. Subrogation
55.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.

HOME CONTENTS INSURANCE POLICY
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 3

1. Definitions
1.1. Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
1.2. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.3. Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
1.4. Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.5. Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to you or your family.
1.6. Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
1.7. Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
1.8. High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
1.9. Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
1.10. Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.11. Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
1.12. Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
1.13. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.14. Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
1.15. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.16. Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.17. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.18. Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.19. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.20. Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 60 consecutive days.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.2. Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.3. Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.4. Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
2.5. The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

3. Sanctions
3.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

4. How to read this document
4.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
4.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
4.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

5. Change of address
5.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
5.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

6. Geographical limits
6.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
6.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

7. Interest
7.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

8. Subrogation
8.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
8.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

9. Governing law
9.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
9.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

10. Communication
10.1. We will communicate with you in English.
10.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

11. Alternative accommodation
11.1. If your home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, we will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
11.2. We will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with you.
11.3. Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

12. Assignment
12.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

13. Contents temporarily removed
13.1. Your contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
13.2. Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of your family.

14. Automatic renewal
14.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
14.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

15. Tenant's improvements
15.1. If you rent the home, we will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that you installed and are responsible for.
15.2. This cover applies only to improvements you paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

16. Electronic documents
16.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
16.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
16.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

17. Severability
17.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

18. Salvage
18.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
18.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

19. Waiver
19.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

20. Escape of Water
20.1. We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
20.2. The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
20.3. We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
20.4. We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

21. Instalment agreements
21.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
21.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

22. Reasonable precautions
22.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
22.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

23. Compensation scheme
23.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
23.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

24. Arbitration
24.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
24.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

25. Third-party administrators
25.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
25.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

26. Taxes
26.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
26.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

27. Customer support
27.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
27.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

28. Theft
28.1. We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
28.2. The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
28.3. The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
28.4. We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
28.5. We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
28.6. We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

29. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
29.1. We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
29.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
29.3. The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
29.4. We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
29.5. We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

30. Flood
30.1. We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
30.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.
30.3. The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
30.4. We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

31. Discounts
31.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
31.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

32. Claims documents
32.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
32.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

33. Inflation
33.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
33.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

34. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
34.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

35. Premium payment
35.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
35.2. If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

36. Data protection
36.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
36.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
36.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

37. Complaints
37.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
37.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
37.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

38. Currency
38.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
38.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

39. Changes in circumstances
39.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
39.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

40. Payment of claims
40.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
40.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

41. Freezer contents
41.1. We will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
41.2. We will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

42. Other insurance
42.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
42.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

43. General exclusions
43.1. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
43.2. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
43.3. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
43.4. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
43.5. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

44. Joint policyholders
44.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
44.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

45. Locks and keys
45.1. If the keys to your home are lost or stolen, we will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
45.2. The most we will pay under this clause is $300 for any one claim.

46. Making a claim
46.1. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
46.2. You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
46.3. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

47. Duty of fair presentation
47.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
47.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
47.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

1. Definitions
1.1. Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
1.2. Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
1.3. Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 3,000 metres.
1.4. Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
1.5. Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 6 months before the policy start date.
1.6. Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
1.7. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.2. Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $150 per claim.
2.3. Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.4. Travel Delay: limit $300 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
2.5. The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

3. Personal liability
3.1. We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
3.2. This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
3.3. The most we will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

4. Market conditions
4.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

5. Optional cover: Travel Delay
5.1. We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
5.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
5.3. We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

6. Rental car excess
6.1. If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
6.2. This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

7. Trip Cancellation
7.1. We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
7.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
7.3. The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $200 per incident.
7.4. We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
7.5. We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

8. Emergency Medical Expenses
8.1. We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
8.2. The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
8.3. The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
8.4. We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
8.5. We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
8.6. We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

9. General exclusions
9.1. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
9.2. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

10. Making a claim
10.1. You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
10.2. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
10.3. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

11. Change of address
11.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
11.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

12. Changes in circumstances
12.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
12.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

13. Third-party administrators
13.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
13.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.
