RENTERS CONTENTS PROTECTION
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 3

1. Definitions
1.1. Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
1.2. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.3. Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
1.4. Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.5. Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to you or your family.
1.6. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.7. Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
1.8. Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
1.9. High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
1.10. Home means the private residence at the address shown in the schedule.
1.11. Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.12. Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
1.13. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.14. Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
1.15. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.16. Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.17. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.18. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.19. Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 45 consecutive days.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Theft: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.2. Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
2.3. Accidental Damage: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.4. Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

3. Flood
3.1. We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
3.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
3.3. The most we will pay for Garden items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
3.4. We will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for your area had been issued before the policy started.

4. Escape of Water
4.1. We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
4.2. The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $2,000 per incident.
4.3. We will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
4.4. We will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

5. Optional cover: Accidental Damage
5.1. We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
5.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
5.3. The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $750 per incident.
5.4. We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
5.5. We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

6. Theft
6.1. We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
6.2. The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
6.3. The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
6.4. We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
6.5. We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
6.6. We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

7. General exclusions
7.1. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
7.2. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
7.3. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
7.4. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

8. Making a claim
8.1. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
8.2. You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
8.3. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

9. Reasonable precautions
9.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
9.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

10. Electronic documents
10.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
10.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
10.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

11. Exchange of information
11.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
11.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

12. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
12.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

13. Discounts
13.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
13.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

14. Third-party administrators
14.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
14.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

15. Automatic renewal
15.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
15.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

16. Interest
16.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

17. Renewal
17.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
17.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

18. Payment of claims
18.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
18.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

19. Joint policyholders
19.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
19.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

20. Other insurance
20.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
20.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

21. Data protection
21.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
21.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
21.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

22. Alternative accommodation
22.1. If your home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, we will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
22.2. We will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with you.
22.3. Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

23. Records and evidence
23.1. You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
23.2. Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
23.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

24. Assignment
24.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

25. Complaints
25.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
25.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
25.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

26. Sanctions
26.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

27. Cooperation
27.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
27.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

28. Taxes
28.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
28.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

29. Customer support
29.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
29.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

30. Notices
30.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
30.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

31. Tenant's improvements
31.1. If you rent the home, we will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that you installed and are responsible for.
31.2. This cover applies only to improvements you paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

32. Changes in circumstances
32.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
32.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

33. Cancellation
33.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
33.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
33.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

34. Fraud
34.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
34.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

35. Severability
35.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

36. Compensation scheme
36.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
36.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

37. Freezer contents
37.1. We will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
37.2. We will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

38. Subrogation
38.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
38.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

39. Change of address
39.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
39.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

40. How to read this document
40.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
40.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
40.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

41. Geographical limits
41.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
41.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

42. Inflation
42.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
42.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

43. Governing law
43.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
43.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

44. Market conditions
44.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

45. Duty of fair presentation
45.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
45.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
45.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

46. Premium payment
46.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
46.2. If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

47. Communication
47.1. We will communicate with you in English.
47.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

48. Accessibility
48.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

49. Arbitration
49.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
49.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

50. Garden and outdoor cover
50.1. We will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
50.2. We will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

51. Recovery of costs
51.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

52. Claims documents
52.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
52.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

53. Interpretation
53.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
53.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
53.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

54. Environmental commitment
54.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
54.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

55. Waiver
55.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

56. Salvage
56.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
56.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

57. Instalment agreements
57.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
57.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

58. Contents temporarily removed
58.1. Your contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
58.2. Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of your family.

59. Locks and keys
59.1. If the keys to your home are lost or stolen, we will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
59.2. The most we will pay under this clause is $500 for any one claim.

60. Currency
60.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
60.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

4.1. We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
4.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
4.3. The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
4.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
4.5. We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

5. Breakdown
5.1. We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
5.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
5.3. The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
5.4. We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
5.5. We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

6. General exclusions
6.1. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
6.2. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
6.3. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
6.4. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

7. Making a claim
7.1. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
7.2. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
7.3. You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.

8. Geographical limits
8.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
8.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

9. Claims documents
9.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
9.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

10. Complaints
10.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
10.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
10.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

11. Transferring the plan
11.1. You may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling us in writing.
11.2. The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

12. Accessibility
12.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

13. Inflation
13.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
13.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

14. Discounts
14.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
14.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

15. Joint policyholders
15.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
15.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

16. Fraud
16.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
16.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

17. How to read this document
17.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
17.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
17.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

18. Third-party administrators
18.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
18.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

19. Replacement devices
19.1. If we cannot repair your device economically, we will replace it with a replacement device.
19.2. Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
19.3. Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

20. Changes in circumstances
20.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
20.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

21. Taxes
21.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
21.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

22. Recovery of costs
22.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

23. Duty of fair presentation
23.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
23.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
23.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

24. Premium payment
24.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
24.2. If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

25. Exchange of information
25.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
25.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

26. Salvage
26.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
26.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

27. Electronic documents
27.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
27.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
27.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

28. Compensation scheme
28.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
28.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

29. Change of address
29.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
29.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

30. Governing law
30.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
30.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

31. Other insurance
31.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
31.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

32. Software support
32.1. Our helpline can give advice on setting up and using your device.
32.2. Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

33. Renewal
33.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
33.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

34. Communication
34.1. We will communicate with you in English.
34.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

35. Currency
35.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
35.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

36. Arbitration
36.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
36.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

37. Instalment agreements
37.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
37.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

38. Cancellation
38.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
38.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
38.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

39. Reasonable precautions
39.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
39.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

40. Environmental commitment
40.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
40.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

41. Customer support
41.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
41.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

42. Sanctions
42.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

43. Interpretation
43.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
43.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
43.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

44. Repair process
44.1. After a claim is accepted, we will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
44.2. We aim to return repaired devices within 15 business days of receiving them.

45. Waiver
45.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

46. Subrogation
46.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
46.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

47. Payment of claims
47.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
47.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

48. Data and backups
48.1. We are not responsible for recovering or restoring any data, software or settings stored on your device.
48.2. You should back up your data regularly and before sending the device for repair.

49. Cooperation
49.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
49.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

50. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
50.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

51. Severability
51.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

52. Assignment
52.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

53. Data protection
53.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
53.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
53.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

54. Market conditions
54.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

55. Automatic renewal
55.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
55.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

56. Notices
56.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
56.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

57. Interest
57.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

58. Unrecoverable devices
58.1. If a device is found after we have replaced it, the found device becomes our property and must be sent to us.
58.2. We may block devices reported as lost or stolen so that they cannot be used on mobile networks.

59. Records and evidence
59.1. You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
59.2. Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
59.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

GROUP HEALTH CASH PLAN
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 3

1. Definitions
1.1. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.2. Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
1.3. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.4. Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
1.5. Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
1.6. Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
1.7. Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
1.8. Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
1.9. Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
1.10. Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
1.11. Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
1.12. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.13. Replacement period means 12 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
1.14. Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.

2. Limits and deductible
2.1. Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.2. Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
2.3. Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
2.4. Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

3. Sanctions
3.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

4. Compensation scheme
4.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
4.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

5. Leaving the plan
5.1. Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
5.2. Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

6. Waiver
6.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

7. Claims documents
7.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
7.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

8. Cooperation
8.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
8.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

9. Duty of fair presentation
9.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
9.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
9.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

10. Taxes
10.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
10.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

11. Change of address
11.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
11.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

12. Vision Care
12.1. We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
12.2. The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
12.3. We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
12.4. We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

13. Eligibility
13.1. Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
13.2. Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

14. Optional cover: Hearing Care
14.1. We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
14.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
14.3. The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
14.4. We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

15. Renewal
15.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
15.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

16. Subrogation
16.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
16.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

17. Currency
17.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
17.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

18. Dental Care
18.1. We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
18.2. No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
18.3. The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
18.4. The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
18.5. We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
18.6. We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

19. Therapy Services
19.1. We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
19.2. The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
19.3. We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
19.4. We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

20. Discounts
20.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
20.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

21. Inflation
21.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
21.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

22. How to read this document
22.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
22.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
22.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

23. Fraud
23.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
23.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

24. Instalment agreements
24.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
24.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

25. Complaints
25.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
25.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
25.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

26. Environmental commitment
26.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
26.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

ELECTRONICS CARE PLAN
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 2

1. Definitions
1.1. Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
1.2. Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
1.3. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any service fee, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.4. Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by us.
1.5. Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
1.6. Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
1.7. Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.8. Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
1.9. Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.10. Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
1.11. Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
1.12. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.13. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.14. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.15. Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
1.16. Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.17. Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

2. Limits and service fee
2.1. Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
2.2. Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
2.3. Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $149 per claim.
2.4. The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

3. Breakdown
3.1. We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
3.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
3.3. The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
3.4. We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
3.5. We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

4. Accidental Damage
4.1. We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
4.2. The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
4.3. The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $300 per incident.
4.4. We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
4.5. We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

5. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
5.1. We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
5.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
5.3. The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
5.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
5.5. We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

6. General exclusions
6.1. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
6.2. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
6.3. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
6.4. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.

7. Making a claim
7.1. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
7.2. You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
7.3. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

8. Premium payment
8.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
8.2. If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

9. Changes in circumstances
9.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
9.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

10. Renewal
10.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
10.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

11. Replacement devices
11.1. If we cannot repair your device economically, we will replace it with a replacement device.
11.2. Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
11.3. Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

12. Duty of fair presentation
12.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
12.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
12.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

13. Instalment agreements
13.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
13.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

14. Cancellation
14.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
14.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
14.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

15. Assignment
15.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

16. Communication
16.1. We will communicate with you in English.
16.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

17. Records and evidence
17.1. You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
17.2. Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
17.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

18. Data and backups
18.1. We are not responsible for recovering or restoring any data, software or settings stored on your device.
18.2. You should back up your data regularly and before sending the device for repair.

19. Cooperation
19.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
19.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

20. Repair process
20.1. After a claim is accepted, we will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
20.2. We aim to return repaired devices within 15 business days of receiving them.

21. Unrecoverable devices
21.1. If a device is found after we have replaced it, the found device becomes our property and must be sent to us.
21.2. We may block devices reported as lost or stolen so that they cannot be used on mobile networks.

22. Inflation
22.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
22.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

23. Currency
23.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
23.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

24. Interpretation
24.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
24.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
24.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

25. Market conditions
25.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

26. Customer support
26.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
26.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

27. Payment of claims
27.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
27.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

28. Environmental commitment
28.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
28.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

RENTERS CONTENTS PROTECTION
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 2

1. Definitions
1.1. Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
1.2. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.3. Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.

1.5. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.6. Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
1.7. Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
1.8. High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
1.9. Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.10. Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
1.11. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.12. Unoccupied means not lived in by you or a member of your family for more than 60 consecutive days.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Theft: limit $40,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.2. Escape of Water: limit $15,000 per incident; excess $1,000 per claim.
2.3. Accidental Damage: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.4. Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

3. Premium payment
3.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
3.2. If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

4. Freezer contents
4.1. We will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
4.2. We will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

5. Compensation scheme
5.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
5.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

6. Complaints
6.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
6.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
6.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

7. Alternative accommodation
7.1. If your home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, we will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
7.2. We will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with you.
7.3. Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

8. Discounts
8.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
8.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

9. Theft
9.1. We will pay for contents stolen from your home.
9.2. The most we will pay for High-risk items under this section is $1,000 per incident.
9.3. The most we will pay for Bicycles under this section is $500 per incident.
9.4. We will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
9.5. We will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
9.6. We will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

10. Notices
10.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.

11. Currency
11.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
11.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

12.1. We will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to your contents inside the home.
12.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
12.3. The most we will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
12.4. We will not pay for damage caused by pets.
12.5. We will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

14.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

15. Electronic documents
15.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
15.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
15.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

16. Flood
16.1. We will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering your home.
16.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.

18. Escape of Water
18.1. We will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
18.2. The most we will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.

22.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

24.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
24.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

25. Market conditions
25.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

26.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
26.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
26.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

27.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
27.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

28. General exclusions
28.1. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
28.2. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
28.3. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
28.4. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
28.5. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

29. Contents temporarily removed
29.1. Your contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
29.2. Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of your family.

31.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
31.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

32. Arbitration
32.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
32.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

33. Garden and outdoor cover
33.1. We will pay for plants, trees and shrubs in the garden of the home that are damaged by fire, lightning or theft.
33.2. We will not pay for damage caused by frost, storms, drought or animals.

34. Making a claim
34.1. You must notify us of a claim within 21 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
34.2. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
34.3. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

35. Reasonable precautions
35.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
35.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

1.7. Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
1.8. Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
1.9. Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
1.10. Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
1.11. Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
1.12. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.13. Replacement period means 12 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
1.14. Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.

2. Limits and deductible
2.1. Dental Care: limit $1,500 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.2. Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.
2.3. Therapy Services: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $75 per claim.
2.4. Hearing Care: limit $1,000 per treatment; deductible $150 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the deductible is then deducted from the result.

3. Sanctions
3.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

4. Compensation scheme
4.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
4.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

5. Leaving the plan
5.1. Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.
5.2. Claims for treatment received before cover ended may be submitted up to 90 days afterwards.

6. Waiver
6.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

7. Claims documents
7.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
7.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

8. Cooperation
8.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
8.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

9. Duty of fair presentation
9.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
9.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
9.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

10. Taxes
10.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
10.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

11. Change of address
11.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
11.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

12. Vision Care
12.1. We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
12.2. The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
12.3. We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
12.4. We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

13. Eligibility
13.1. Employees who work at least 20 hours a week are eligible to join the plan from their first day of employment.
13.2. Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

14. Optional cover: Hearing Care
14.1. We will reimburse hearing tests and hearing aids.
14.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
14.3. The most we will pay for Hearing accessories under this section is $150 per treatment.
14.4. We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

15. Renewal
15.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
15.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

16. Subrogation
16.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
16.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

17. Currency
17.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
17.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

18. Dental Care
18.1. We will reimburse the cost of dental treatment provided by a licensed dentist.
18.2. No cover applies under this section to any treatment that happens within the first 90 days after the policy start date.
18.3. The most we will pay for Major restorative work under this section is $500 per treatment.
18.4. The most we will pay for Orthodontics under this section is $800 per treatment.
18.5. We will not pay for treatment that is mainly cosmetic, such as whitening or veneers. This exclusion does not apply to treatment needed to repair damage caused by an accident.
18.6. We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

19. Therapy Services
19.1. We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
19.2. The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $300 per treatment.
19.3. We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
19.4. We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

20. Discounts
20.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
20.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

21. Inflation
21.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
21.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

22. How to read this document
22.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
22.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
22.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

23. Fraud
23.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
23.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

24. Instalment agreements
24.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
24.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

25. Complaints
25.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
25.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
25.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

26. Environmental commitment
26.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
26.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

27. Third-party administrators
27.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
27.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

28. Notices
28.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
28.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

29. Interpretation
29.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
29.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
29.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

30. General exclusions
30.1. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
30.2. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
30.3. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
30.4. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

31. Automatic renewal
31.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
31.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

32. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
32.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

33. Joint policyholders
33.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
33.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

34. Accessibility
34.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

35. Interest
35.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

36. Cancellation
36.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
36.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
36.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

37. Appeals
37.1. If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
37.2. An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
37.3. We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

38. Governing law
38.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
38.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

39. Coordination of benefits
39.1. If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
39.2. You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

40. Reasonable precautions
40.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
40.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

41. Making a claim
41.1. You must notify us of a claim within 90 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
41.2. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
41.3. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

42. Other insurance
42.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
42.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

43. Recovery of costs
43.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

44. Market conditions
44.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

45. Data protection
45.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
45.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
45.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

46. Changes in circumstances
46.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
46.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.
