Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 2

1. Definitions
1.1. Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
1.2. Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
1.3. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.4. Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,000 metres.
1.5. Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
1.6. Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
1.7. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.8. Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
1.9. Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.10. Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 12 hours.
1.11. Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.12. Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
1.13. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.14. Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
1.15. Trip means a journey that starts and ends in your home country during the policy period.
1.16. Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $75 per claim.
2.2. Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $10,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
2.3. Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.4. Travel Delay: limit $500 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

3. Payment of claims
3.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
3.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 15 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

4. Environmental commitment
4.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
4.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

5. Trip Cancellation
5.1. We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
5.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 10 days after the policy start date.
5.3. The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
5.4. We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
5.5. We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

6. Cooperation
6.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
6.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

7. Renewal
7.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
7.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

8. Reasonable precautions
8.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
8.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

9. Waiver
9.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

10. Sanctions
10.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

11. Other insurance
11.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
11.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

12. Personal liability
12.1. We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
12.2. This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
12.3. The most we will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

13. Complaints
13.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
13.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
13.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

14. Recovery of costs
14.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

15. Salvage
15.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
15.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

16. Arbitration
16.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
16.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

17. Joint policyholders
17.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
17.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

18. Subrogation
18.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
18.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

19. Severability
19.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

20. Inflation
20.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
20.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

21. Premium payment
21.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
21.2. If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

22. Legal expenses abroad
22.1. We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
22.2. We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

23. Geographical limits
23.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
23.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

24. Notices
24.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
24.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

25. Market conditions
25.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

26. Change of address
26.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
26.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

27. Taxes
27.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
27.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

28. Cancellation
28.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
28.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
28.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

29. Instalment agreements
29.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
29.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

30. Optional cover: Travel Delay
30.1. We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
30.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
30.3. We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

31. Currency
31.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
31.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

32. Data protection
32.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
32.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
32.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

33. Rental car excess
33.1. If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
33.2. This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

34. Governing law
34.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
34.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

35. Baggage and Personal Belongings
35.1. We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
35.2. The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
35.3. The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
35.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
35.5. We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
35.6. We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

36. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
36.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

37. Emergency Medical Expenses
37.1. We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
37.2. The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
37.3. The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
37.4. We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
37.5. We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
37.6. We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

38. How to read this document
38.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
38.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
38.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

39. Claims documents
39.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
39.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

40. Electronic documents
40.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
40.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
40.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

41. Duty of fair presentation
41.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
41.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
41.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

42. Communication
42.1. We will communicate with you in English.
42.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

43. Fraud
43.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
43.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

44. Missed departure
44.1. We will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach your destination if you arrive too late to board your booked transport because public transport fails.
44.2. You must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

45. Compensation scheme
45.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
45.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

46. Interpretation
46.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
46.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
46.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

47. Interest
47.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

48. Automatic renewal
48.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
48.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

49. Assignment
49.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

50. Discounts
50.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
50.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

51. Repatriation
51.1. If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
51.2. We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

52. Emergency assistance
52.1. Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
52.2. You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
52.3. The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

53. Exchange of information
53.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
53.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

54. General exclusions
54.1. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
54.2. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
54.3. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
54.4. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
54.5. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
54.6. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

55. Making a claim
55.1. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
55.2. You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
55.3. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

56.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
56.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

57.1. You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
57.2. Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
57.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

58. Third-party administrators
58.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
58.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

59. Changes in circumstances
59.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
59.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

ELECTRONICS CARE PLAN
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 1

1. Definitions
1.1. Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
1.2. Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
1.3. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any service fee, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.4. Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by us.
1.5. Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
1.6. Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
1.7. Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
1.8. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.9. Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
1.10. Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
1.11. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.12. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.13. Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.14. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.15. Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
1.16. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.17. Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

2. Limits and service fee
2.1. Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $49 per claim.
2.2. Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
2.3. Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
2.4. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the service fee is then deducted from the result.

3. Optional cover: Theft and Loss
3.1. We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
3.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
3.3. The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
3.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
3.5. We will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

4. Changes in circumstances
4.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
4.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

5. Recovery of costs
5.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

6. Premium payment
6.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
6.2. If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

7. Transferring the plan
7.1. You may transfer the plan to a new owner of the device by telling us in writing.
7.2. The remaining term of the plan transfers with the device; the term does not restart.

8. Breakdown
8.1. We will repair or replace your device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
8.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
8.3. The most we will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $120 per incident.
8.4. We will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
8.5. We will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

9. Communication
9.1. We will communicate with you in English.
9.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

10. Joint policyholders
10.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
10.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

11. Repair process
11.1. After a claim is accepted, we will send a prepaid mailer or book a courier collection.
11.2. We aim to return repaired devices within 10 business days of receiving them.

12. Customer support
12.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
12.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

13. Geographical limits
13.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
13.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

14. Cancellation
14.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
14.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $30.
14.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

15. Instalment agreements
15.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
15.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

16. Waiver
16.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

17. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
17.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

18. Duty of fair presentation
18.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
18.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
18.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

19. Notices
19.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
19.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

20. Data and backups
20.1. We are not responsible for recovering or restoring any data, software or settings stored on your device.
20.2. You should back up your data regularly and before sending the device for repair.

21. Replacement devices
21.1. If we cannot repair your device economically, we will replace it with a replacement device.
21.2. Replacement devices may be a different colour and may be refurbished to an as-new standard.
21.3. Accessories are replaced only if they were lost or damaged in the same incident as the device.

22. Interest
22.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

23. Renewal
23.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
23.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

24. Fraud
24.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
24.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

25. Accidental Damage
25.1. We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
25.2. The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
25.3. The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $250 per incident.
25.4. We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
25.5. We will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than us or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if we approved the repair in writing beforehand.

26. Reasonable precautions
26.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
26.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

27. General exclusions
27.1. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
27.2. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
27.3. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
27.4. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
27.5. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

28. Making a claim
28.1. You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
28.2. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
28.3. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Customer (Colm): Hi, I need to make a claim on policy H644601 under Theft and Loss for a laptop.
Agent: Sure. When did the policy start and what covers does your schedule show?
Customer (Colm): It started on Thursday, July 23, 2026. The schedule lists Accidental Damage, Breakdown, Theft and Loss, and extensions: none.
Agent: When did the incident happen, and what happened?
Customer (Colm): On Sunday, July 26, 2026. Colm had left the laptop in a parked car while visiting a museum. The car was locked and the laptop was in the closed boot, out of sight.
Agent: Anything else we should know?
Customer (Colm): The retailer's receipt was uploaded with the claim.

9.2. Contractors, agency workers and employees on unpaid leave of more than three months are not eligible.

10. Therapy Services
10.1. We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
10.2. The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
10.3. We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.

14. Governing law

16. Assignment

17. Severability
17.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

18. Subrogation
18.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
18.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

19. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
19.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

20.1. We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
20.2. The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $150 per treatment.
20.3. We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
20.4. We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

21. Dependants
21.1. You may enrol dependants at the start of each plan year or within 30 days of a qualifying life event.
21.2. Benefits paid for dependants count towards the same annual limits as your own claims.

22. Changes in circumstances
22.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
22.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

23. Environmental commitment
23.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
23.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

24. Reasonable precautions
24.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
24.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

25. Other insurance
25.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
25.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

26. Sanctions
26.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

27. Currency
27.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
27.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

28.1. Cover ends on the day your employment ends or the day you stop being eligible, whichever is earlier.

29.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.

30. Notices

31.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

34.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
34.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

35.1. If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
35.2. You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

36. General exclusions
36.1. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
36.2. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
36.3. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
36.4. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
36.5. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

37. Cooperation
37.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
37.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

38. Compensation scheme
38.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
38.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

39. Geographical limits
39.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
39.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

40. Customer support
40.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
40.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

41. Payment of claims

41.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

42. Automatic renewal
42.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
42.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

43. Third-party administrators
43.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
43.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

44. Electronic documents
44.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
44.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
44.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

45. Making a claim

47.1. We will communicate with you in English.
47.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

48. Accessibility
48.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

55.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

56.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
56.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

57.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
57.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

58.2. Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of your family.

Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 1

1. Definitions
1.1. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.2. Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.3. Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
1.4. Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
1.5. Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,000 metres.
1.6. Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
1.7. Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
1.8. Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
1.9. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.10. Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which you received treatment or advice in the 12 months before the policy start date.
1.11. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.12. Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.13. Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
1.14. Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 6 hours.
1.15. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.16. Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.17. Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
1.18. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
1.19. Trip means a journey that starts and ends in your home country during the policy period.
1.20. Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

2. Limits and excess
2.1. Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $1,500 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.2. Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
2.3. Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
2.4. Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
2.5. Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

3. Automatic renewal
3.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
3.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

4. Instalment agreements
4.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
4.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

5. Severability
5.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

6. Cancellation
6.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
6.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
6.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

7. Optional cover: Travel Delay
7.1. We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
7.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
7.3. We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

8. Salvage
8.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
8.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

9. Inflation
9.1. We may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
9.2. Any adjustment will be shown in your renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

10. Geographical limits
10.1. Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
10.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

11. Renewal
11.1. We will write to you at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
11.2. We are not obliged to offer renewal.

12. Environmental commitment
12.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
12.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

13. Baggage and Personal Belongings
13.1. We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
13.2. The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $400 per incident.
13.3. The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
13.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
13.5. We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
13.6. We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

14. Emergency assistance
14.1. Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
14.2. You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
14.3. The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

15. Third-party administrators
15.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
15.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

16. Premium payment
16.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
16.2. If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

17. Interpretation
17.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
17.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
17.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

18. Communication
18.1. We will communicate with you in English.
18.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

19. Discounts
19.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
19.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

20. Repatriation
20.1. If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
20.2. We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

21. Electronic documents
21.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
21.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
21.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

22. Recovery of costs
22.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

23. Waiver
23.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

24. Customer support
24.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
24.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

25. Other insurance
25.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
25.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

26. Missed departure
26.1. We will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach your destination if you arrive too late to board your booked transport because public transport fails.
26.2. You must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

27. Interest
27.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

28. Reasonable precautions
28.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
28.2. You must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

29. Emergency Medical Expenses
29.1. We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
29.2. The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
29.3. The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
29.4. We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
29.5. We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
29.6. We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

30. Payment of claims
30.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
30.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

31. Sanctions
31.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

32. Currency
32.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
32.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

33. Rental car excess
33.1. If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
33.2. This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

34. Arbitration
34.1. If we accept a claim but disagree with you about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
34.2. Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against us.

35. Claims documents
35.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
35.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

36. Taxes
36.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
36.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

37. Changes in circumstances
37.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
37.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

38. Compensation scheme
38.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
38.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

39. Cooperation
39.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
39.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

40. Trip Cancellation
40.1. We will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if you must cancel the trip for a reason beyond your control.
40.2. No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
40.3. The most we will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
40.4. We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
40.5. We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

41. Personal liability
41.1. We will pay damages you become legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
41.2. This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
41.3. The most we will pay under this section is $2,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

42. Market conditions
42.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

43. Joint policyholders
43.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
43.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

44. Change of address
44.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
44.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

45. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
45.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

46. Subrogation
46.1. We will be entitled to take over and conduct in your name the defence or settlement of any claim.
46.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

47. How to read this document
47.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
47.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
47.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

48. Accessibility
48.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

49. Exchange of information
49.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
49.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

50. Notices
50.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
50.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

51. Data protection
51.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
51.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
51.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

52. Records and evidence
52.1. You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
52.2. Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
52.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

53. Duty of fair presentation
53.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
53.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
53.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

54. General exclusions
54.1. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
54.2. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
54.3. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

55. Complaints
55.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
55.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
55.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

56. Legal expenses abroad
56.1. We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
56.2. We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

57. Fraud
57.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
57.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

58. Governing law
58.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
58.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

59. Assignment
59.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

60. Making a claim
60.1. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
60.2. You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
60.3. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

Agent: Sure. When did the policy start and what covers does your schedule show?
Customer (Maya): It started on Wednesday, January 8, 2025. The schedule lists Baggage and Personal Belongings, Emergency Medical Expenses, Trip Cancellation, and extensions: none.
Agent: When did the incident happen, and what happened?
Customer (Maya): On Wednesday, November 19, 2025. The trip was cancelled because Maya was admitted to hospital a week before departure.
Agent: Anything else we should know?
Customer (Maya): The return flight was scheduled for the following week. The trip was booked through an online travel agent. The destination was a coastal town Maya had visited before.
Agent: Noted. I am logging this claim today, Monday, November 24, 2025, the first time it has been reported to us. Our adjuster has assessed the loss at $82.

23.2. Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

24. Notices
24.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
24.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

25. Market conditions
25.1. If the replacement item is no longer available, we will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

26. Change of address
26.1. You must tell us within 30 days if you change your address.
26.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

27. Taxes
27.1. The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
27.2. If the tax rate changes, we may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

28. Cancellation
28.1. You can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
28.2. After the first 14 days you can cancel at any time; we will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $25.
28.3. We can cancel this policy by giving you 30 days' written notice to the last address we hold.

29. Instalment agreements
29.1. If you pay by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
29.2. Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

30. Optional cover: Travel Delay
30.1. We will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if your outbound departure is delayed.
30.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
30.3. We will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

31. Currency
31.1. All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
31.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

32. Data protection
32.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
32.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
32.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

33. Rental car excess
33.1. If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
33.2. This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

34. Governing law
34.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
34.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

35. Baggage and Personal Belongings
35.1. We will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to your baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
35.2. The most we will pay for Valuables under this section is $250 per incident.
35.3. The most we will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
35.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
35.5. We will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
35.6. We will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

36. Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
36.1. A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

37. Emergency Medical Expenses
37.1. We will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
37.2. The most we will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $250 per incident.
37.3. The most we will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $500 per incident.
37.4. We will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
37.5. We will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in your schedule.
37.6. We will not pay for any claim arising from your being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

38. How to read this document
38.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
38.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
38.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

39. Claims documents
39.1. You must provide, at your own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence we reasonably ask for.
39.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

40. Electronic documents
40.1. We will send documents by email unless you ask for paper copies.
40.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.
40.3. Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

41. Duty of fair presentation
41.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
41.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
41.3. If you give incorrect information carelessly, we may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

42. Communication
42.1. We will communicate with you in English.
42.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

43. Fraud
43.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
43.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

44. Missed departure
44.1. We will pay reasonable additional travel and accommodation costs to reach your destination if you arrive too late to board your booked transport because public transport fails.
44.2. You must allow enough time to reach the departure point, and must obtain written confirmation of the delay from the transport operator.

45. Compensation scheme
45.1. We are covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
45.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

46. Interpretation
46.1. Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
46.2. Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
46.3. Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

47. Interest
47.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

48. Automatic renewal
48.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
48.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

49. Assignment
49.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

50. Discounts
50.1. Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
50.2. If a condition for a discount stops being met, we may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

51. Repatriation
51.1. If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.
51.2. We will decide the method of transport and the time of repatriation after speaking to the treating doctor.

52. Emergency assistance
52.1. Our emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
52.2. You must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
52.3. The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

53. Exchange of information
53.1. To prevent fraud, we may check the details you give against public records and industry databases.
53.2. We may contact previous insurers to confirm your claims history.

54. General exclusions
54.1. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
54.2. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
54.3. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
54.4. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
54.5. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
54.6. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.

55. Making a claim
55.1. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
55.2. You must notify us of a claim within 14 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
55.3. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

56. Customer support
56.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
56.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

57. Records and evidence
57.1. You should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
57.2. Where proof of value is missing, we may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
57.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

58. Third-party administrators
58.1. We may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on our behalf.
58.2. Any company we appoint must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

59. Changes in circumstances
59.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
59.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

60. Accessibility
60.1. This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

EMPLOYEE HEALTH BENEFITS PLAN: SUMMARY PLAN DESCRIPTION
Issued by Synthetic Policy Office 2

1. Definitions
1.1. Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by us, before any deductible, limit or sublimit is applied.
1.2. Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
1.3. Dependant means your spouse or partner, or a child under 21 who is enrolled in the plan.
1.4. Family means your spouse or partner and any children who live with you.
1.5. Frames means spectacle frames bought without new lenses.
1.6. Hearing accessories means batteries, chargers and cleaning kits.
1.7. Hearing aid replacement period means 36 months from the purchase of hearing aids funded by the plan.
1.8. Limit means the most we will pay for all claims under a section arising from one treatment.
1.9. Major restorative work means crowns, bridges, root canal treatment and implants.
1.10. Massage therapy means sports massage, massage therapy and reflexology.
1.11. Network provider means a practitioner or clinic that has an agreement with us to provide treatment.
1.12. Orthodontics means braces and clear aligners.
1.13. Plan year means the twelve months starting on your coverage start date.
1.14. Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in your schedule.
1.15. Premium means the amount you must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
1.16. Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
1.17. Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
1.18. Registered practitioner means a practitioner registered with the professional body for their discipline.
1.19. Replacement period means 24 months from the date of your last eyewear claim.
1.20. Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows your details, the covers you bought and any extensions.
1.21. Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.

2.1. Dental Care: limit $2,000 per treatment; deductible $50 per claim.
2.2. Vision Care: limit $500 per treatment; deductible $25 per claim.

3. Governing law
3.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
3.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

4.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

5.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.

5.4. We will not pay for replacement hearing aids bought within the hearing aid replacement period.

6. Appeals
6.1. If we decline all or part of a claim, you may appeal in writing within 60 days of the decision.
6.2. An appeal will be reviewed by someone who was not involved in the original decision.
6.3. We will give you a written decision on the appeal within 30 days.

7. Vision Care
7.1. We will reimburse eye tests and prescription eyewear.
7.2. The most we will pay for Frames under this section is $120 per treatment.
7.3. We will not pay for eyewear without prescription lenses.
7.4. We will not pay for a further eyewear claim within the replacement period.

8. Sanctions
8.1. We will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose us to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

9. Salvage
9.1. When we replace an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes our property.
9.2. If stolen property is recovered after we have paid a claim, you must tell us and either return the payment or give us the property.

10. Data protection
10.1. We will use the personal information you provide to administer this policy and to handle claims.
10.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
10.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

11. Therapy Services
11.1. We will reimburse physiotherapy, osteopathy and counselling provided by a registered practitioner.
11.2. The most we will pay for Massage therapy under this section is $200 per treatment.
11.3. We will not pay for treatment of an injury covered by workers' compensation.
11.4. We will not pay for treatment by a practitioner who is not registered with the relevant professional body.

12. Other insurance
12.1. If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, we will pay only our proportionate share.
12.2. You must tell us about any other insurance that covers the same loss when you make a claim.

13.1. If a treatment is also covered by another plan, we will pay only the part of the cost that the other plan does not pay.
13.2. You must tell us about any other plan that covers you or your dependants.

14.1. Where practical, we will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
14.2. You may ask for a new part instead, and we will tell you whether any additional cost would apply.

17.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
17.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

18.6. We will not pay for treatment by a provider outside the plan's network. This exclusion does not apply to emergency treatment for sudden severe pain.

19. General exclusions
19.1. We will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
19.2. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
19.3. We will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits us from paying.
19.4. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
19.5. We will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
19.6. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

20. Customer support
20.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
20.2. Outside these hours you can leave a message and we will call back on the next working day.

21. Making a claim
21.1. You must notify us of a claim within 60 days of the treatment. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
21.2. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
21.3. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

22. Automatic renewal
22.1. Unless you tell us otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details we hold.
22.2. You can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting our helpline.

23. Payment of claims
23.1. We will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in your name.
23.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 10 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

24. Waiver
24.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

25. Premium payment
25.1. You must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
25.2. If an instalment is not paid within 7 days of its due date, we may cancel the policy after giving notice.

1. Definitions

4. Data and backups

4.2. You should back up your data regularly and before sending the device for repair.

5. Complaints
5.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
5.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
5.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

6.1. We will replace your device if it is stolen or lost.
6.2. This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in your schedule.
6.3. The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $50 per incident.
6.4. We will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.

7. Interest
7.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

8. How to read this document
8.1. This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
8.2. Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
8.3. Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

9. Severability
9.1. If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

10. Accidental Damage
10.1. We will repair or replace your device if it is accidentally damaged.
10.2. The most we will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
10.3. The most we will pay for Wearables under this section is $250 per incident.
10.4. We will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.

11. Notices
11.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
11.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

12. General exclusions
12.1. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
12.2. We will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by you.
12.3. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.

13. Customer support
13.1. Our helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.

15. Duty of fair presentation
15.1. You must answer all questions we ask honestly and to the best of your knowledge.
15.2. If you give incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, we may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.

16. Other insurance

17. Assignment

18.2. We may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

20.1. If our medical adviser agrees it is necessary, we will arrange and pay for you to be brought home.

21.2. You must tell us if your email address changes.

22. Recovery of costs
22.1. If we pay a claim that is later found not to be covered, we may ask you to repay the amount.

23.1. If we do not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean we have given up the right to enforce it later.

27.1. We will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

28.1. You must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.

30.2. We aim to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents we need.

32. Currency

32.2. Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

33.1. If you hire a car during the trip, we will reimburse any excess you must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.

35.2. We may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

37.1. You must tell us as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
37.2. We may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

38.2. If we cannot meet our obligations, you may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

39. Cooperation
39.1. You must give us all the help and information we reasonably need to settle a claim.
39.2. You must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without our written permission.

40.4. We will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before you bought the policy.
40.5. We will not pay for cancellation because you no longer wish to travel.

41. Personal liability

41.2. This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
41.3. The most we will pay under this section is $2,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

43. Joint policyholders
43.1. Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
43.2. A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

44.2. We may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

46. Subrogation

46.2. We can take action in your name to recover any payment we make from anyone responsible for the loss.

50. Notices
50.1. Any notice we give under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address we hold.
50.2. Notices from you should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

51.2. We will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
51.3. You can ask for a copy of the personal information we hold by writing to our data protection officer.

52.3. We may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

54.2. We will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
54.3. We will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.

55.1. If you have a complaint, you should first contact our customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
55.2. We will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
55.3. If you remain dissatisfied, you may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

56.1. We will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for your injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
56.2. We will not pay legal costs unless our legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

57. Fraud
57.1. If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, we will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
57.2. We may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

58. Governing law
58.1. This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
58.2. Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

59. Assignment
59.1. You cannot transfer your interest in this policy to anyone else without our written consent.

60. Making a claim
60.1. You must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
60.2. You must notify us of a claim within 30 days of the incident. We will not pay any claim notified after that time.
60.3. We may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
